policy.managedReceiptScope: Any operation that creates, replaces, or removes source-derived MemPalace representations must preserve exact source/output lineage through managed receipts.
policy.retirementMeaning: Retire the unmanaged mutation surface, not the user-facing capability; retain a read-only or receipt-aware replacement.
policy.explicitExclusionMeaning: The state is not a source-derived drawer representation and must use a named, separately testable ownership, backup, and audit contract.
policy.historicalBoundary: No disposition fabricates write-time receipts for old rows. Any replay emits a new historical-recovery run receipt with the original source evidence linked as input.

entries.surface: Legacy collection migration and palace-directory swap
entries.managedRepresentation: Preserve or rebuild the receipt journal and prove every current source manifest before the replacement directory is swapped in.
entries.reason: A collection rebuild can otherwise preserve rows while silently severing their authoritative receipt lineage.

entries.surface: Repair deletion of corrupt drawer IDs
entries.managedRepresentation: Publish invalidations or successor manifests for every authoritative receipt affected by a deleted row.
entries.reason: Deleting a represented row without updating lineage makes an otherwise complete receipt report a permanent unexplained missing output.

entries.surface: Repair replay that recreates collections and upserts recovered rows
entries.managedRepresentation: Bind backup identity, recovered rows, replacement collections, and superseded receipts into one attended recovery run.
entries.reason: A replay changes the represented store wholesale and therefore must preserve the authoritative source/output contract.

entries.surface: Direct Chroma SQLite sequence-metadata correction
entries.reason: Physical sequence metadata is not a source-derived drawer, but changing it still needs an exclusive lock, backup, before/after evidence, and an operation receipt.

entries.surface: Duplicate-drawer deletion
entries.managedRepresentation: For every approved deletion, publish a successor or invalidation that explains why the old exact output no longer belongs to its source representation.
entries.reason: Deleting IDs without revising exact manifests turns intentional cleanup into unexplained receipt loss.

entries.surface: Sweeper JSONL-to-drawer ingestion
entries.managedRepresentation: Use the existing source and message identities through managed adapter ingestion and exact rewrite recovery.
entries.reason: The path already has deterministic source identity and is a normal source-derived write.

entries.surface: Compression-generated closet records
entries.managedRepresentation: Emit derived-output receipts that bind source manifests, model identity, configuration digest, and exact generated closets.
entries.reason: Generated summaries are derived memory outputs whose reproducibility depends on both source state and model/configuration.

entries.surface: Diary file drawer and closet ingestion
entries.managedRepresentation: Preserve the diary source lock while routing drawer and closet writes through managed ingestion and rewrite recovery.
entries.reason: A diary file is a normal versioned source and should have the same exact representation proof as project and conversation files.

entries.surface: LLM closet purge and regeneration
entries.managedRepresentation: Publish a successor derived-output receipt binding source rows, model/configuration, and exact generated output hashes.
entries.reason: Regeneration purges old derived outputs before replacement and therefore needs the same durable predecessor snapshot as other rewrites.

entries.surface: Global topic-tunnel JSON topology registry
entries.reason: Topic topology is operational graph state, not evidence that a source is represented as drawers.

entries.surface: Knowledge-graph entity and triple SQLite writes
entries.reason: Graph entities and temporal triples need graph-specific lineage and completeness; forcing them into drawer receipts would misstate both representations.

entries.surface: MCP drawer add, update, and delete tools
entries.managedRepresentation: Require a logical source identity and publish create, supersession, or deletion receipts inside the existing palace lock.
entries.reason: Serialization proves ordering, not provenance or the completeness of the resulting source representation.

entries.surface: MCP diary writer
entries.managedRepresentation: Route the tool through managed diary ingestion and the shared lock/recovery boundary.
entries.reason: The former diary path bypassed both source receipts and the drawer tools' common mutation wrapper.

entries.surface: Project configuration, entity, and origin sidecar files
entries.reason: These files configure or audit ingestion; their hashes can influence run receipts, but they are not represented memory outputs themselves.

entries.surface: Automatic Chroma quarantine, HNSW configuration, and SQLite repair during backend open
entries.retirementTarget: Opening becomes read-only; each mutation moves to an explicit locked, backup-backed maintenance command with an operation receipt.
entries.reason: A read/open operation must not silently change durable state or make backup and rollback timing unknowable.

entries.surface: Public write-capable ChromaBackend and palace.get_collection access
entries.retirementTarget: Keep raw mutation primitives private to receipt-aware core code and expose read-only public collection views.
entries.reason: Any public raw handle can bypass source identity, recovery snapshots, and receipt publication by construction.

entries.surface: PalaceContext non-dry pass-through writes outside managed_adapter_ingest
entries.retirementTarget: Preserve read-only context use; require managed_adapter_ingest for every non-dry adapter mutation.
entries.reason: The pass-through mode is a supported bypass around all source receipt and recovery guarantees.

entries.surface: Project and conversation miner branches that permit receipt_store=None
entries.retirementTarget: Require a ReceiptStore for non-dry core mining; preserve receiptless behavior only for explicitly read-only/dry execution.
entries.reason: An optional receipt parameter leaves the canonical miner capable of silently returning to best-effort destructive rewrites.

entries.surface: Duplicate legacy repair implementation in cli.py
entries.retirementTarget: Route the CLI to one receipt-aware repair service and remove the duplicate direct implementation.
entries.reason: Two repair implementations can drift on locking, backup, receipt, and verification behavior.

entries.surface: MCP cache that directly gets or creates Chroma collections
entries.retirementTarget: Make the transport consume a private read facade and explicit receipt-aware mutation service; never create durable collection state as a read-side cache effect.
entries.reason: Transport caching should not own database creation or expose a second write path around the canonical backend boundary.

entries.surface: Global config, onboarding state, hook logs, exports, and split-output files
entries.reason: These files are inputs, exports, or operational evidence rather than current palace representations and must not inflate drawer completeness denominators.
